story_type: x-class solar flare filmed by five observatories at once, raw power in space
hook: An explosion on the Sun, caught by five telescopes at once.
narration: This is an explosion on the Sun, caught by five telescopes at once.
On March twenty-ninth, 2014, the Sun fired off an X-class flare.
X-class is the top of the scale, the most intense kind of flare.
Flares like this can cause radio blackouts near Earth, cutting into airplane, ship and military communications.
NASA's IRIS spacecraft had been aimed at this exact spot, hoping to catch one. It was the first X-class flare it ever saw.
Another spacecraft tracked the flare's material rising more than three thousand miles above the surface.
[short pause] And in New Mexico, a ground telescope got lucky. The flare hit at the best time of day to watch.
outcome: It went down as the best observed solar flare of all time.

title: Solar flare caught by 5 telescopes
description:
On March 29, 2014, the Sun released an X-class flare that was watched by NASA's SDO, IRIS and RHESSI spacecraft, Japan's Hinode and the Dunn Solar Telescope in New Mexico, making it the best observed flare of its time.
